## Introduction

This document demonstrates how to combine Markdown text with executable R code chunks in Quarto. R chunks use the built-in `knitr` engine, so no extra `jupyter` field is needed in the header - just start a chunk with `` ```{r} ``.

## Heritability by Trait

Broad-sense heritability ($H^2$) tells us what fraction of the variation we see in a trait is actually due to genetics, as opposed to the environment. Below, we simulate a small set of heritability estimates across several trial years for a handful of traits.

```{r}
#| label: fig-heritability
#| fig-cap: "Simulated broad-sense heritability by trait across trial years"
#| warning: false

library(ggplot2)

set.seed(42)
traits <- rep(c("Yield", "Plant Height", "Disease Score", "Days to Maturity"), each = 5)
year <- rep(2020:2024, times = 4)
heritability <- pmin(pmax(runif(20, 0.25, 0.9), 0), 1)

df <- data.frame(trait = traits, year = year, heritability = heritability)

ggplot(df, aes(x = year, y = heritability, color = trait)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Heritability Trends by Trait",
    x = "Trial Year",
    y = expression(paste("Broad-sense heritability (", H^2, ")")),
    color = "Trait"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Takeaway

Yield tends to show lower and noisier heritability than more visually/directly measured traits like plant height, since it's influenced by more environmental factors and gene-by-environment interactions.
